note: Synthetic fixture manually synchronized from the platform acceptance-gate roster for the self-contained STORY-413, STORY-420, and EPIC135 tests; platform-level consistency remains owned by platform-doctor.
recoveredFrom: The nine groups were reconstructed from the 2026-08-17 closeout session's own green table, then each was re-run on 2026-08-19 and kept only if it still executes. Where a group's command had moved, the entry carries what runs today rather than what ran then.

groups.title: Engine unit and integration suite
groups.proves: Every engine behaviour with a test, including the protocol and workspace kernels.

groups.title: Engine P1 gate train
groups.proves: The full ordered gate roster: format, lint, typecheck, build, suite, portal, trust, archive, sbom, licences, vulnerabilities, source, sibling independence, lifecycle, offline, governance, workspace, privacy, roots, ci, verification map, history, and the proof budget.

groups.title: Guard mutation proof
groups.proves: Every declared guard is killed by its registered mutation -- that each guard has a proof rather than a claim.

groups.title: Release consistency
groups.proves: Version, badges, release note, translation pins and tag reachability agree across the committed tree. Judges the committed tree, so it runs after the commit.

groups.title: Platform layout and deployment freshness
groups.proves: Partition topology, engine copy alignment, installed adapter markers, trust archive and consumer roots.

groups.title: Every partition validates
groups.proves: Each chain replays, and its derived views match what the current engine projects. This is the group a view-shape change makes red until every chain is recovered.

groups.title: Product repository gates
groups.proves: The product repository that carries gates and is in MVP scope. Narrowed from DS+AOS to DS alone by Owner ruling on 2026-08-19: the MVP is the workflow and helper repositories, AOS integration is explicitly out of scope, and the AOS red (TCRN-CROSS-INC-234 -- three imports of the engine's MCP facade retired in v0.11.18) is a known exception to be repaired after MVP. Restoring AOS to this group is part of closing INC-234, not a separate decision. The pairing rationale this group originally carried -- a cross-repo change left one repository red for a day because only the author's gate got run -- is precisely what INC-234 caught again, and is why AOS returns here rather than leaving quietly.

narrowedBy.scope: MVP phase only; product-gates judges TCRN-Design-System alone
narrowedBy.restoration: closing TCRN-CROSS-INC-234 restores TCRN-AOS to the product-gates group
